tagline: The old Red Trail, taking the slow way beside the interstate.
intro: From the Mandan Depot on Main Street the old road runs west beside Interstate 94 through Almont, New Salem, Glen Ullin, Hebron and Richardton to Dickinson, a slower way across the same country. Before there were highways, cross-country trails went by color names, and this one, the Red Trail, ran from Seattle to New York City before it became Highway 10. Custer used the route on his march west.
Glen Ullin got its name from a railroad land agent, who set the Gaelic word for valley in front of a name out of a Thomas Campbell poem.

moments.title: Salem Sue
moments.text: On School Hill at New Salem stands a fiberglass Holstein 38 feet high, paid for in 1974 by local farmers and residents and visible for several miles.

moments.title: Sims
moments.text: A coal town of 1883 that the railroad straightened away from in 1947, leaving a Lutheran church and a parsonage that locals say a pastor's wife still haunts.

moments.title: Assumption Abbey
moments.text: Benedictine monks who began on the north shore of Devils Lake moved to Richardton in 1899, and their priory was raised to an abbey in 1903.

practical: The 2021 state tourism page called the road blacktop but noted gravel between New Salem and Glen Ullin and on the Curlew Loop spur toward Almont.
